title: How Long Would You Last Falling Into Neptune? #shorts
description_hook: You drop into Neptune's cloud tops at -201 °C, with nothing to land on and no oxygen to breathe. The clock starts now.

beats.say: How long would you last falling into Neptune? You drop into the cloud tops. It's minus 201 degrees Celsius.
beats.img: a tiny human silhouette tumbling into a vast deep-blue sea of clouds on an ice giant planet, faint distant sunlight, freezing haze

beats.say: Gravity is 1.12 times Earth's, so you feel almost normal. But there's no solid surface. Nothing to stand on. You just keep falling.
beats.img: looking straight down through endless layers of pale blue cloud on a gas giant, no ground in sight, a lone falling figure small in the center

beats.say: Then the wind grabs you. More than 2,000 kilometers per hour up here at cloud level. You spin like a leaf.
beats.img: violent streaks of white methane clouds racing across a cobalt blue planetary atmosphere, a small dark figure caught and spinning in the jet stream

beats.say: You gasp. The air is mostly hydrogen and helium. No oxygen at all. One or two breaths, and you're out.
beats.img: a dim blue haze of thin cold gas with the outline of a person drifting unconscious, darkness gathering at the edges of the frame

gumi.say: Gumi's odds: zero. Scientists think below you: over 1,000 bars and hot, icy fluid.
